HARD governor holds — refusals that never reach a human

The Loss Adjustment Governor is a separate system from the Adjuster-LLM and can reject. These runs settled at :hold without ever passing the interrupt-before #{:request-approval} handoff, so no approver was ever offered the chance to wave them through. Every rule and detail below is the governor's own violation map.

Rollout-phase holds — a different thing from a governor refusal

These are the adjustment.phase gate deferring a write that the current rollout phase has not enabled yet. They are written to the ledger as :t :governor-hold like a compliance refusal, but their :violations vector is empty and they carry a :phase-reason instead. Nothing is wrong with the proposal — the actor is simply not allowed to do that yet. The build-time invariant in assert-hard-holds! counts these separately for exactly this reason.

Human approval handoffs (interrupt-before :request-approval)

Runs the governor cleared but that no phase may auto-commit. The actor genuinely pauses here — :status is :interrupted until a human resumes it. The escalation reason is the actor's own: :actuation means the op issues a real valuation report an insurer or insured will rely on, :phase-approval means the phase has not made it auto-eligible, and :low-confidence means the advisor itself came in under governor/confidence-floor (0.6).

Approver attribution — measured, not assumed

Probed at render time: for every approved run, does the record the commit actually wrote still contain the approver? The probe looks for any key mentioning “approv” on the persisted record rather than a hard-coded :approved-by, so if the store is later changed this page reports the change instead of repeating a stale claim. Rows are keyed by thread id — [op subject] is not a unique join key.

ThreadOpSubjectApprover (resume input)RegisterKeyRecord written?Approver retained?Retained under
m1-assess:jurisdiction/assessmatter-1adjuster-ito:assessmentsmatter-1yesyesapproved-by = adjuster-ito
p2-screen:conflict/screenparty-2adjuster-ito:conflictsparty-2yesyesapproved-by = adjuster-ito
p6-screen:conflict/screenparty-6adjuster-ito:conflictsparty-6yesyesapproved-by = adjuster-ito
m1-finalize:valuation/finalizematter-1adjuster-ito:valuationsJPN-VAL-000000yesNO — dropped by the store—
m3-assess:jurisdiction/assessmatter-3adjuster-ito:assessmentsmatter-3yesyesapproved-by = adjuster-ito

Measured this run: 4 of 5 approved commits retained the approver, and 1 did not — :valuation/finalize → :valuations. Those effects are applied from a value the store rebuilds itself, so the :approved-by the operation put on the record’s payload never lands in the register. This is stated rather than omitted: silently leaving the approver out would make “nobody approved it” and “the store did not keep it” look identical to a reader.

The persisted audit ledger does not carry an approver key on any fact — the commit fact records :actor (the actor-id that ran the operation, op-1), which is not the human who approved it. The approver above was read from each run’s own :approval-granted audit fact, which is real output of this run but is not persisted anywhere by the actor.

Jurisdiction spec-basis catalog & honest coverage

The governor rejects any assessment that cites no official source for its jurisdiction. Coverage is reported honestly: a jurisdiction absent from adjustment.facts/catalog has no spec-basis, full stop — the advisor must not invent one. Of the 2 jurisdiction(s) this run’s matters actually use, 1 are covered and ATL is not — which is exactly why the assessment for that matter HARD-held above.
